findings.title: OS Command Injection via Service Name Argument Injection (CTF Flag)
findings.description: The /check_service endpoint passes the service_name JSON field directly to check_service.sh via shell=True without proper sanitization. The script supports a '-t custom' mode that executes arbitrary commands. While basic shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $, backtick) are filtered, spaces and single-quotes are allowed. By injecting '-t custom' as a type argument, an attacker can execute arbitrary commands. Single-quoting the command allows multi-word commands to bypass the single-argument limitation. The application runs as root, providing full system compromise.

reproduction.command: curl -s -X POST http://172.17.0.1:33153/check_service -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"service_name": "-t custom \'cat FLAG.txt\'"}'
